study_identification_part.si_4_title: Accommodating Site Variation In Neuroimaging Data Using Normative And Hierarchical Bayesian Models

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: Hierarchical Bayesian Linear Model (HBLM) with site as a random effect; Hierarchical Bayesian Gaussian Process Model (HBGPM) adding a Gaussian process for age.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: In a hierarchical linear version of the model, site is modeled hierarchically, resulting in a random effect for site ('Hierarchical Bayesian Linear Model, HBLM'). In a non-linear version of the model, a Gaussian Process for age is added to test whether performance is increased if the model is also able to capture non-linear effects between age and thickness of the cortical region ('Hierarchical Bayesian Gaussian Process Model, HBGPM').
nm2_1_modeling_methods.location: Bayer2022.pdf.md: Section 3.4 Site as a predictor in a Hierarchical Bayesian Model

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: Cortical thickness measures of 34 bilateral regions (averaged left/right) and average cortical thickness across all 34 regions.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: For the current study, we focused on cortical thickness measures of the 34 bilateral regions (averaged between left and right hemisphere) of the Desikian Killiany atlas parcellation (Desikan et al., 2006) as a part of the FreeSurfer (Fischl et al., 2004) output and the average cortical thickness across all 34 regions.

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: Predictors include age, sex, and site (site modeled as a predictor/random effect).
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: normative models describing the association between age, sex, and cortical thickness measures can be modeled on data comprising site effects using a hierarchical Bayesian linear mixed model with a Gaussian Process term
